name: Tokyo Skytree from Sumida Park
short_description: Use the riverside promenade as a clean foreground for a vertical view of Tokyo Skytree across eastern Tokyo.

shooting_area.name: Sumida Park riverside promenade
shooting_area.standing_instruction: Remain on the public riverside promenade. Keep the path, railings, benches and emergency access clear, and do not climb or lean equipment over barriers.
shooting_area.verification_note: The area is based on the reference photo's embedded coordinate and official Sumida Park visitor information. It has not been field checked.

shot_guide.bearing_method: rounded from the 108.6-degree image direction embedded in the reference photo metadata
shot_guide.phone_camera_suggestion: Start with the main 1x camera. Use a modest crop or 2x lens only after confirming the tower remains sharp and the riverside context is still visible.
shot_guide.composition_instruction: Keep the Skytree vertical, use the promenade and nearby river edge as leading context, and leave breathing room above the antenna.
shot_guide.composition_short_instruction: Keep Skytree vertical and leave clear sky above the antenna.
shot_guide.expected_view: Tokyo Skytree rising beyond the Sumida riverside from the Asakusa side.
field_checks_needed: Confirm the coordinate falls on an unobstructed public path.
Compare 28 mm, 37 mm and 50 mm framing.
Verify the final bearing from the practical standing position.
Check whether trees, river works or seasonal events obstruct the view.

timing_and_light.primary_recommendation: For a daylight match, try approximately 60 to 120 minutes before sunset when the tower can retain detail against the sky. Exact direction and color vary by season.
timing_and_light.alternate_recommendation: Blue hour can add Skytree illumination, but the lighting design and start time vary by date.
timing_and_light.lighting_direction_note: The camera faces east-southeast. Late-afternoon light arrives from behind and to the right in many seasons, but the exact angle changes through the year.
timing_and_light.subject_lighting_note: Tokyo Skytree publishes a changing lighting calendar. Check the official schedule on the visit date for an evening version.

access.address: 7-1 Asakusa and surrounding riverside, Taito City, Tokyo, Japan
access.line: Tokyo Metro Ginza Line / Tobu Isesaki Line / Tsukuba Express
access.cost_note: No admission charge is published for this public park composition.
access.published_hours: GO TOKYO describes the riverside park but does not publish a closing time on the reviewed page.

accessibility.summary: The exact step-free route to the selected riverside area has not been verified.
accessibility.note: Use current station and park accessibility information and follow riverside closures.

conditions.crowd_note: GO TOKYO notes particularly heavy use during cherry blossom season and major riverside events. This general rating is an editorial estimate.
conditions.safety_note: Stay behind riverside barriers, keep the shared path clear and avoid stepping backward toward bicycles or path edges.

rules_and_respect.site_type: public riverside park and shared promenade
guidance: Keep the promenade and river access clear.
Follow current park signs, closures and event controls.
Do not place equipment beyond railings or in planted areas.
Avoid photographing identifiable park users without permission.
Do not assume tripod permission; use one only if current rules permit and space is clear.
Pack out all waste and avoid bright lights near other visitors.
rules_and_respect.editorial_rule: ViewRoam must not present tripod or commercial-shoot permission as confirmed.

live_conditions.title: Skytree lighting changes by date
live_conditions.message: The target reference is a daylight frame. For an illuminated version, check the official Tokyo Skytree lighting calendar on the visit date.

seasonal_notes.note: Cherry blossoms add foreground color but GO TOKYO reports substantial seasonal crowding.
Expect later light, humidity, haze and riverside events.
Clearer air can strengthen tower detail and sky separation.
Low humidity and earlier sunset can make both daylight and blue-hour versions practical.
